india.headline: Kolkata RISE conclave links four CSIR laboratories with industry and startups
india.summary: The sixth RISE conclave brought together CSIR laboratories working on minerals, medicine, materials and machines. The government said the programme produced eight MoUs, four technology transfers, two product launches and a new facility inauguration.
india.why: The concrete test is whether these lab-to-market agreements turn publicly funded research into products, manufacturing capability and regional startup growth beyond India's largest hubs.

india.headline: National biodiversity meeting asks local committees to move from registration to action
india.summary: At a two-day meeting in Chandigarh, the National Biodiversity Authority urged states and Union territories to align procedures with the amended biodiversity law and make more than 276,000 Biodiversity Management Committees function effectively on the ground.
india.why: India already has a vast local conservation network on paper; implementation will shape habitat protection, community participation and the fair sharing of benefits from biological resources.

india.headline: National workshop focuses on rebuilding safe landscapes for India's vultures
india.summary: A Panchkula workshop convened conservation agencies, veterinarians and researchers around vulture-safe zones, captive breeding, technical capacity and community participation, alongside International Vulture Awareness Day observances.
india.why: Vultures are exceptionally efficient scavengers, so restoring their populations is tied to carcass disposal, disease risk and the resilience of whole landscapes rather than to one species alone.

india.headline: At least three killed as rescuers search collapsed Delhi student residence
india.summary: A five-storey building used as student accommodation collapsed in Satya Niketan. The Indian Express reported at least three deaths and seven patients taken to AIIMS Trauma Centre while rescue work continued.
india.why: The disaster again puts building safety, enforcement and emergency access in dense urban neighbourhoods under scrutiny, particularly where residential properties house large numbers of students.

india.headline: Rajnath Singh to visit Sri Lanka for defence and maritime-security talks
india.summary: India announced that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will visit Sri Lanka from September 8 to 10 with a senior delegation for talks with the country's leadership and engagement with the Indian diaspora.
india.why: Defence coordination with Sri Lanka matters to India's neighbourhood strategy, Indian Ocean awareness and the balance between security cooperation and Colombo's other external relationships.

world.headline: Iran claims a strike on a US vessel in the Strait of Hormuz; Washington denies it
world.summary: Iran said it hit an unmanned American vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, a claim the US military rejected. The dispute followed US strikes on three Iranian oil tankers after missiles targeted US Navy warships, according to AP.
world.why: Claims and counterclaims in this narrow shipping corridor can raise the chance of miscalculation and immediately affect expectations for energy flows, insurance and maritime security.

world.headline: US envoys meet Zelenskyy in Kyiv after talks with Putin produce no announced breakthrough
world.summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner made their first official visit to Ukraine for talks with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. European national-security advisers joined later, after the envoys' lengthy Moscow meeting with Vladimir Putin yielded no public breakthrough.
world.why: The sequence tests whether Washington can bridge positions held by Kyiv, Moscow and European capitals without treating security guarantees or territorial questions as bilateral details.

world.headline: Anak Krakatau eruption closes eight Indonesian airports and disrupts mass travel
world.summary: Anak Krakatau erupted early Sunday without reported casualties or evacuation orders. By evening, AP reported eight airport closures, roughly 170,000 affected passengers and 1,558 cancelled flights, including 963 involving Jakarta.
world.why: The disruption shows how a localized volcanic event can propagate rapidly through a tightly connected aviation network even when communities near the volcano avoid immediate loss of life.

world.headline: Saxony-Anhalt votes in a major test of Germany's firewall against the AfD
world.summary: Voters in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt cast ballots in an election that could give the far-right Alternative for Germany its first postwar state-government opportunity. The final outcome was not yet available in the cited report.
world.why: Coalition arithmetic here will indicate whether mainstream parties can sustain their refusal to govern with the AfD as the party's regional electoral strength grows.

world.headline: Worker rescued after ten days in Nepal tunnel as glacier-linked flood toll mounts
world.summary: Rescuers brought Chinese hydropower worker Lu Haitao out alive after ten days trapped in a 225-metre tunnel. AP reported more than 1,300 deaths and nearly 4,900 people missing after floods believed to have followed a glacier collapse.
world.why: The rescue is a rare success inside a much larger disaster that connects Himalayan cryosphere hazards with infrastructure exposure, downstream warning systems and cross-border workforces.

domain1.title: AdaptiveISP: Learning an Adaptive Image Signal Processor for Object Detection
domain1.authors: Yujin Wang, Tianyi Xu, Fan Zhang, Tianfan Xue, and Jinwei Gu
domain1.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (NeurIPS 2024)
domain1.summary: AdaptiveISP replaces a single fixed image-processing chain with a policy that chooses a short, scene-dependent sequence of differentiable ISP modules and their parameters to improve a downstream detector under a computation budget.
domain1.problem: A conventional camera ISP is tuned to make images look broadly pleasing, while a vision detector cares about task-relevant evidence. One fixed pipeline is also asked to handle scenes whose noise, illumination, colour and dynamic range differ sharply, creating a mismatch between camera processing and machine perception.
domain1.difficulty: The design space is mixed and combinatorial: the system must decide which modules to run, in what order, with what continuous parameters and when to stop. A useful policy also has to receive a signal from a fixed detector, remain trainable through image operations and avoid buying marginal accuracy with an impractical amount of processing.
domain1.idea: Treat ISP construction as a sequential decision problem instead of selecting one static architecture. A learned policy observes the evolving image, selects an operator and its settings, and can stop early, letting easy scenes use a compact path while difficult scenes receive additional task-guided processing.
domain1.method: The authors formulate adaptive ISP control as a Markov decision process. At each step, a policy examines features of the current image and chooses from a toolbox of differentiable image-processing modules together with continuous parameters; a STOP action ends the chain. The chosen operations transform the input before it reaches a fixed, pretrained object detector. Deep reinforcement learning optimizes the discrete structure decisions and continuous controls using a reward tied to detection quality, while a computational-cost term discourages needlessly long or expensive chains. Because the policy acts sequentially, it can build different operator orders for different scenes rather than merely tune the gains of a fixed graph. Experiments on low-light object detection compare these adaptive paths with conventional and learned fixed ISP baselines and inspect how often modules are selected.
domain1.results: On the LOD benchmark with a fixed pretrained YOLOv3 detector, the authors report 71.4 mAP at IoU 0.5, compared with 70.1 for their optimized fixed ISP. Their analysis also finds that the policy uses only a few modules for most inputs, supporting the claim that scene adaptation can improve task accuracy without applying the full toolbox every time.
domain1.care: The paper is a useful blueprint for camera systems built for perception rather than display: pipeline topology itself becomes conditional compute. But its evidence is detector- and benchmark-specific, reinforcement-learning training adds complexity, the operator set remains largely in the RGB image domain, and better detector reward does not guarantee visually pleasing or artifact-free images for people.
learn: How to express a camera pipeline as a sequential policy with a STOP decision.
Why task loss can select different processing than perceptual image-quality loss.
How a runtime penalty turns variable pipeline depth into a conditional-compute tradeoff.
What to measure when comparing adaptive processing with a carefully optimized fixed baseline.

domain2.title: CoDISP: Exploring Compressed Domain Camera ISP with RGB-guided Encoder
domain2.authors: Molin Zhang, Soumendu Majee, Chengyu Wang, Seok-Jun Lee, and Hamid Sheikh
domain2.field: Mobile camera ISP and memory optimization
domain2.summary: CoDISP learns a compact camera-domain representation and performs demosaicing, denoising and registration on that latent, targeting the bandwidth and memory pressure created by moving full-resolution raw frames through a mobile imaging pipeline.
domain2.problem: High-resolution and burst photography force mobile systems to store and move large raw tensors between ISP stages. That memory traffic constrains latency, power and the number of frames available for computational photography, yet lossy compression can discard sensor information that later restoration tasks need.
domain2.difficulty: Raw colour-filter-array data and display-ready RGB images have different sampling structures, and useful compression must preserve information for several downstream tasks rather than one reconstruction score. Training directly from raw data is also restricted by the limited scale and diversity of paired high-resolution camera datasets.
domain2.idea: First learn a compact latent representation from abundant RGB imagery, then teach a raw encoder to imitate that representation. Camera processing can subsequently operate on the fixed-size latent, making the RGB model a source of supervision for a sensor-domain compressor without requiring an equally large raw corpus.
domain2.method: Training proceeds in three stages. An RGB encoder-decoder is first trained on approximately 300,000 256-by-256 crops from OpenImages so that a low-channel latent retains enough visual information for reconstruction. A raw encoder is then initialized and guided to produce the same latent representation from simulated colour-filter-array measurements, using an L1 alignment objective against the RGB encoder's features. Finally, task-specific decoders or processing heads learn to work directly from that compressed code for demosaicing, single-frame and multi-frame denoising, and affine registration. The paper studies two-channel latents with spatial resolutions chosen for compression ratios of four and six, evaluates Bayer and Tetra sampling, and describes the representation as fixed-rate rather than entropy-coded. Public Kodak, CLIC and MCM images support reconstruction tests, while an internal high-resolution collection is used for downstream proof-of-concept experiments.
domain2.results: Across the public reconstruction sets, the paper reports that compression ratios of four and six retain performance close to corresponding non-compressed processing while materially shrinking intermediate storage. The same learned representation supports proof-of-concept single- and multi-frame denoising and registration, suggesting that its usefulness is not confined to decoding an RGB image.
domain2.care: Moving ISP work into a compact latent could reduce one of mobile imaging's less visible bottlenecks: memory traffic. The evidence is exploratory, however. Some raw mosaics and noise are simulated, downstream tests use internal data, the code is fixed-rate rather than entropy-coded, and the study does not establish end-to-end device latency, energy use or quality across commercial sensors.
learn: How RGB pretraining can supervise a raw-sensor encoder when paired raw data is scarce.
Why fixed-rate latent size and entropy-coded file size answer different engineering questions.
How one compressed representation can be tested across reconstruction, denoising and alignment.
Which dataset and hardware gaps remain before a mobile deployment claim is convincing.

outside1.title: A postsynaptic burst controls the Hebbian strengthening of human synapses
outside1.authors: Franz X. Mittermaier, Thilo Kalbhenn, Ran Xu, et al.
outside1.summary: Recordings from living human cortical slices show how a sequence resembling neuronal UP and DOWN states can prepare a synapse for stronger transmission, while a postsynaptic burst determines whether that transient gain becomes lasting potentiation.
outside1.problem: Cellular accounts of memory rely heavily on rodents and simplified spike-timing rules. The authors ask how naturalistic changes in membrane potential affect transmitter release at connected human cortical neurons, and which event converts a temporary increase in synaptic strength into a durable Hebbian change.
outside1.difficulty: Healthy human cortical circuits cannot be sampled experimentally at will. Viable tissue comes from neurosurgery, connected neuron pairs are rare, axonal voltage is technically difficult to record, and ex vivo stimulation has to isolate presynaptic excitability, release probability and postsynaptic spiking without confusing them.
outside1.idea: A prolonged depolarized UP state can inactivate presynaptic Kv1 potassium channels and broaden the next axonal action potential after a recovery period, transiently increasing release. If that stronger input recruits a postsynaptic burst, the burst acts as a gate that stabilizes potentiation; without it, the synapse tends toward depression.
outside1.method: The team used acute neocortical slices removed during surgery from 33 people treated for refractory epilepsy and 12 treated for tumours. Paired whole-cell recordings from connected layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons measured unitary excitatory postsynaptic potentials, while somato-axonal recordings linked somatic voltage patterns to action-potential width in axons. Controlled depolarizations lasting 50, 200, 500 or 1,000 milliseconds modelled aspects of an UP state, followed by a hyperpolarized interval resembling a DOWN state. Pharmacology and voltage protocols tested the role of slowly recovering Kv1 channels and sodium-channel availability. Longer protocols then paired the enhanced presynaptic input with either successful or absent postsynaptic burst firing to determine which sequence produced persistent potentiation rather than depression.
outside1.results: Depolarizations of 200, 500 and 1,000 milliseconds increased subsequent EPSP amplitude by 11 ± 4%, 15 ± 3% and 19 ± 5%, while 50 milliseconds did not. A 1,000-millisecond depolarization broadened axonal action potentials by 13 ± 2%. Adding an UP-DOWN-like sequence raised potentiation to 27% in 21 recordings, and enhanced inputs recruited postsynaptic spikes in 83 of 163 trials versus 44 of 163 control trials across six experiments.
outside1.care: The work links membrane state, axonal ion-channel kinetics and a cellular learning gate in human tissue, offering a mechanistic bridge between cortical rhythms and plasticity. It is not direct evidence about sleep or memory behaviour: the slices came from surgical patients, network states were imposed electrically, and the number of connected-pair and burst-gating experiments was necessarily limited.
learn: How presynaptic action-potential width changes neurotransmitter release.
Why Kv1 inactivation and sodium-channel recovery favour an UP-then-DOWN sequence.
How a postsynaptic burst can convert short-lived facilitation into stable potentiation.
How evidence from human surgical tissue differs from an in-vivo memory experiment.

outside2.title: Achieving net zero greenhouse gas emissions critical to limit climate tipping risks
outside2.authors: Tessa Möller, Annika Ernest Högner, Carl-Friedrich Schleussner, et al.
outside2.summary: A coupled tipping-element model finds that temporary temperature overshoot is not harmless: risk rises with peak warming and its duration, while reaching and sustaining net-zero greenhouse-gas emissions sharply limits long-run exposure.
outside2.problem: Paris-aligned pathways may exceed 1.5°C before cooling later, but policy discussions often focus on the endpoint and understate what can happen during the overshoot. The study asks how the height, duration and reversal of warming affect the chance of destabilizing major components of the Earth system.
outside2.difficulty: Tipping thresholds, transition speeds and interactions remain deeply uncertain, and the relevant consequences unfold for centuries to millennia. A model must propagate uncertainty across emissions, global temperature, four heterogeneous Earth-system components and their couplings without presenting an unknowable threshold as a precise forecast.
outside2.idea: Evaluate entire warming trajectories rather than only their temperature in 2100. Sampling uncertain thresholds and interaction strengths across many scenarios reveals how every increment and year of overshoot accumulates risk, and why net zero is a physical requirement for stabilizing exposure rather than merely a political milestone.
outside2.method: The authors drive the stylized PyCascades model with emissions trajectories from the PROVIDE v1.2 scenario ensemble and global temperatures emulated by FaIR v1.6.2. Four interacting tipping elements are represented: the Greenland and West Antarctic ice sheets, the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation and the Amazon rainforest. Monte Carlo sampling varies uncertain temperature thresholds, transition times and interaction strengths. The analysis compares pathways with different peak warming, overshoot durations and long-term outcomes, tracking risk through 2300 and, for equilibrium behaviour, over 50,000 years. Scenario groups include low and high overshoots that return below 1.5°C as well as current-policy trajectories. This is a risk framework built from simplified bifurcation dynamics, not a process-resolving Earth-system prediction.
outside2.results: For the 2020 current-policy scenario, the model gives a 45% median chance of at least one tipping event by 2300, with a 10th-to-90th-percentile range of 23–71%. Low overshoots below 0.1°C have a median risk below 1% and a 0–7% range; high overshoots returning below 1.5°C by 2100 have a median of 2% and remain at or below 10%. Risk rises with each additional 0.1°C and accelerates above 2°C.
outside2.care: The paper makes delayed climate action legible as accumulated exposure rather than a reversible temperature detour, strengthening the case for rapid net zero and minimal overshoot. Its percentages should not be read as calibrated forecasts: only four elements are modelled, each uses stylized dynamics, and thresholds, couplings and omitted cascades remain uncertain.
learn: Why peak warming and time above a threshold both matter for tipping risk.
How Monte Carlo sampling carries uncertain thresholds and couplings into risk ranges.
Why returning below 1.5°C does not erase every consequence of an overshoot.
Where a stylized tipping model is informative and where it cannot replace Earth-system simulation.

remember: A static pipeline can be a hidden assumption: AdaptiveISP shows that choosing operations per scene can improve a fixed detector while limiting compute.
Compression is most useful when downstream tasks can stay in the latent domain; repeatedly decoding full-resolution images gives memory savings back.
Temporary state changes can open a window without fixing the outcome: human synapses needed a postsynaptic burst to stabilize transient facilitation.
Climate overshoot has path dependence too; returning below 1.5°C reduces future exposure but cannot guarantee that tipping risks accumulated during the excursion disappear.
Sunday market numbers belong to Friday's completed session, so the date of the observation matters as much as the displayed percentage.
From biodiversity committees to vulture-safe zones, institutional presence is only an input; ecological outcomes depend on local capacity and sustained execution.
takeaways.explore: Trace a shared design question across today's papers: when should a system preserve flexibility, and when should it commit? AdaptiveISP delays commitment to an operator sequence until it sees the scene; CoDISP commits early to a compact representation but tests whether several later tasks remain possible; the synapse paper describes a temporary biochemical window that becomes lasting change only after a postsynaptic burst; and the tipping study warns that crossing a threshold may create dynamics that later cooling cannot simply reverse. For one system you work with, identify its state, its trigger for commitment, the cost of waiting and whether rollback is genuinely available. Then design one measurement that would distinguish reversible adaptation from path-dependent change.
